## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:

Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

124	### 4.2 data_list 解析与 %X 采样率语法
125	
126	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
127	
128	`data_list` 是注册表的查询函数：输入一组「可能带 `%X` 后缀」的数据集名字，输出一组**可直接使用的配置字典**，每个字典额外多一个 `sampling_rate` 键（浮点数 0~1）。它做三件事：
129	
130	1. 用正则从名字末尾剥出 `%X`，换算成 `X / 100`；
131	2. 去掉后缀得到纯代号，去 `data_dict` 查表；
132	3. 查到的配置**浅拷贝**一份，挂上 `sampling_rate` 后收集返回；查不到就抛 `ValueError: do not find ...`。
133	
134	采样发生在**解析之后、训练之前**的加载阶段（见 4.3），`data_list` 本身不读任何文件。
135	
136	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
137	
138	```text
139	输入: ["my_dataset%50", "clevr_mc"]
140	  对每个名字 name:
141	    rate = parse_sampling_rate(name)        # 正则 r"%(\d+)$" 命中末尾 %50 → 0.5；未命中 → 1.0
142	    name  = 去掉末尾 %50                     # "my_dataset"
143	    config = data_dict[name].copy()          # 浅拷贝，不污染注册表
144	    config["sampling_rate"] = rate
145	输出: [ {annotation_path, data_path, sampling_rate: 0.5},
146	       {annotation_path, data_path, sampling_rate: 1.0} ]
147	```
148	
149	采到的样本条数公式（在 4.3 的加载阶段计算）：
150	
151	\[ n_{sampled} = \operatorname{int}\left( N \times rate \right) \]
152	
153	注意 `int()` 是**向下取整**：3 条样本 × 50% = 1.5 → 取 1 条。
154	
155	必须掌握的四个边界情况：
156	
157	| 写法 | 解析结果 | 后果 |
158	| --- | --- | --- |
159	| `my_dataset%50` | rate=0.5 | 正常用一半 |
160	| `my_dataset%150` | rate=1.5 | 解析不报错；加载时 `random.sample(annotations, k>N)` 抛 `ValueError` |
161	| `my_dataset%0` | rate=0.0 | 该数据集贡献 0 条样本（`random.sample(..., 0)` 返回空列表） |
162	| `my_dataset%50v2` | 正则要求 `%数字` 在**末尾**，不命中 | 整串 `my_dataset%50v2` 当作代号查表 → `do not find` |
163	
164	另有一个易踩的坑：`dataset_use` 用逗号分隔多个名字时**不要加空格**。`"a,b"` 没问题，`"a, b"` 会把 `" b"`（带前导空格）当代号去查表而失败。此外 `random.sample` 没有固定随机种子，**同一命令两次运行抽到的子集不同**，做对比实验时需自行在训练脚本里 `random.seed(...)`（待本地验证：`train_qwen.py` 未额外设种子，跨 run 不可复现）。

213	### 4.3 LazySupervisedDataset 加载：从 dataset_use 到 list_data_dict
214	
215	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
216	
217	`LazySupervisedDataset` 是训练时真正的数据集类（继承 `torch.utils.data.Dataset`）。它的 `__init__` 完成「从字符串到样本清单」的全部工作：
218	
219	- 把 `data_args.dataset_use` 按逗号拆开，交给 4.2 的 `data_list` 得到配置列表；
220	- 逐个配置读标注文件（JSONL 逐行、JSON 整体）；
221	- 对 `sampling_rate < 1.0` 的数据集执行 `random.sample` 随机抽取；
222	- 给**每条标注**注入 `data_path` 键（后面 `_build_messages` 用它解析相对媒体路径）；
223	- 把所有数据集的标注按注册顺序**顺序拼接**成 `self.list_data_dict`。
224	
225	「Lazy」体现在：到此为止**不做任何分词与图片读取**，只持有轻量的标注字典列表；`__len__` 就是 `len(list_data_dict)`，真正的张量化发生在训练循环按索引调用 `__getitem__` 时（u5-l3 精读）。
226	
227	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
228	
229	```text
230	__init__(processor, data_args)
231	  ├─ dataset_use.split(",")            # "a%50,b" → ["a%50", "b"]
232	  ├─ data_list(名字列表)               # 查表 + 解析采样率（4.2）
233	  ├─ for data in 配置列表:
234	  │    ├─ 后缀 == "jsonl" ? read_jsonl : json.load      # 按扩展名二分
235	  │    ├─ sampling_rate < 1.0 ?
236	  │    │     random.sample(annotations, int(N × rate))  # 在这里才真正采样
237	  │    └─ for ann in annotations:
238	  │         ann["data_path"] = data["data_path"]         # 逐条注入基准路径
239	  │         （ann 是 list 时对每个子项注入 → packed 样本，见 4.4）
240	  │    list_data_dict += annotations                     # 顺序拼接
241	  ├─ 打印 "Total training samples: N"
242	  ├─ update_processor_pixels(...)       # 把像素预算参数写进 processor（u5-l3 展开）
243	  └─ data_packing ? item_fn=_get_packed_item : item_fn=_get_item   # 决定取样本方式
244	```
245	
246	`data_path` 注入是被下一讲反复引用的关键一步：标注文件里的相对路径之所以能被解析，就是因为加载时每条样本都随身携带了基准目录。`_build_messages` 中用 `Path(source.get("data_path", ""))` 取出它、再与相对路径拼接（参见 [qwen-vl-finetune/qwenvl/data/data_processor.py:L140-L156](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/qwen-vl-finetune/qwenvl/data/data_processor.py#L140-L156) 中的 `_make_abs_paths` 调用）。`data_path` 为空时 `Path("")` 退化为相对当前工作目录解析——这就是 4.1 说「留空需谨慎」的原因。

317	### 4.4 多数据集混合、packed 嵌套注入与长度属性
318	
319	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
320	
321	真实 SFT 往往混合多个数据集。本框架的混合规则非常朴素：
322	
323	- **顺序拼接**：按 `dataset_use` 里代号的书写顺序，逐个数据集把标注 `+=` 到总列表。谁写在前面，谁的样本就排在列表前部。
324	- **逐数据集采样**：`%X` 只作用于它修饰的那一个代号，互不影响。
325	- **packed 样本兼容**：若某个数据集的标注是「桶的列表、桶内又是样本的列表」（u4-l2 讲过的两层结构），加载循环会把 `data_path` 注入到**每个内层子样本**上，保证后续逐样本处理时基准路径不丢失。
326	
327	另外，`__init__` 会依据 `data_args.data_packing` 决定取样本的函数 `item_fn`：开 packing 时用 `_get_packed_item`（整桶取出），否则用 `_get_item`（单样本取出）。这与 u4-l4 的 `pack_data.py` 产出物配套。
328	
329	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
330	
331	```text
332	dataset_use = "a%50,b_pack"
333	list_data_dict = [a 的 5 条] + [b_pack 的若干「桶」(每桶是 list)]
334	                        ↑ 顶层元素类型不统一？没关系：
335	                          data_packing=True 时 _get_packed_item 把「桶」整体取出再逐样本处理
336	                          data_packing=False 时 _get_item 期望顶层元素是普通样本 dict
337	```
338	
339	长度属性（供训练侧做长度分组/装箱参考）：

341	- `lengths`：粗略估计 = 对话文本按空格切词数 + 每个含图样本固定加 128（视觉 token 的近似占位）。

427	
428	- 注册表是一个 63 行的纯 Python 字典文件：每个数据集只有 `annotation_path`（标注文件）与 `data_path`（媒体基准目录）两个键，代号到配置的映射集中在 `data_dict`。

# 数据集注册表与采样率控制

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清 `qwenvl/data/__init__.py` 中数据集注册表的组织方式，以及 `annotation_path` 与 `data_path` 两个字段的分工。
2. 独立把一个自定义数据集（上一讲制作的 `my_dataset.json`）注册进训练框架。
3. 掌握 `%X` 采样率语法：它是如何被解析、何时被执行、有哪些边界坑。
4. 跟踪 `LazySupervisedDataset` 的 `__init__` 流程：从 `--dataset_use` 字符串到一份拼接完成的 `list_data_dict` 标注列表。

本讲是单元四「微调数据准备」的第三讲。上一讲我们搞清了「一条训练样本长什么样」，本讲回答「一堆训练样本如何被框架找到、按比例抽取、混在一起」。

## 2. 前置知识

- **注册表（registry）模式**：框架用一个字典把「数据集名字」映射到「配置信息」。用户在启动脚本里只写名字，框架凭字典查表拿到真实路径。这是许多训练框架（LLaVA 系、mPLUG 系）的通用做法，好处是启动脚本与磁盘路径解耦。
- **标注文件（annotation）与媒体数据（data）分离**：一条样本的 JSON 里只写图片/视频的相对路径，真实文件放在另一个目录。训练时用 `data_path + 相对路径` 拼出绝对路径。这样同一份标注可以配合不同的数据存放位置。
- **JSON 与 JSONL**：JSON 是一个完整数组（一次性 `json.load`）；JSONL 是「每行一个 JSON 对象」的流式格式（逐行 `json.loads`），适合超大标注文件。本框架两种都支持。
- **采样率（sampling rate）**：只想用某个数据集的一部分数据时，按百分比随机抽取，例如 `%50` 表示抽一半。常用于控制多个数据集的混合比例或做小规模冒烟实验。
- **lazy（惰性）加载**：`__init__` 阶段只读入标注列表，不做分词、不加载图片；真正的张量化推迟到训练时按样本索引 `__getitem__` 才发生。这样启动快、内存省。
- 承接上一讲（u4-l2）：你已经知道一条样本由 `image`/`video` 字段（单值或列表）与 `conversations`（human/gpt 交替）构成，`<image>`/`<video>` 占位符与媒体文件按出现顺序一一配对。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 数据集字典：annotation_path 与 data_path 的分工

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

框架为每个数据集定义一个只有两个键的小字典：

- `annotation_path`：**标注文件的路径**，指向一个 `.json` 或 `.jsonl` 文件，里面是样本数组。
- `data_path`：**媒体文件的基准目录**。标注里写的图片/视频路径是相对路径时，就用它拼绝对路径；如果标注里已经是绝对路径，它可以留空字符串。

所有这些小字典再被收进总注册表 `data_dict`，键是数据集的「代号」。训练脚本里 `--dataset_use` 填的就是这些代号，而不是磁盘路径——这正是注册表模式的意义：**脚本里写名字，源码里存路径**。

仓库内置了 5 个示例条目（`cambrian_737k`、`cambrian_737k_pack`、`mp_doc`、`clevr_mc`、`videochatgpt`），值都是 `PATH_TO_XXX` 占位符，需要用户替换成真实路径才能用。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```text
用户视角：
  data/__init__.py
  ├─ CAMBRIAN_737K      = {annotation_path: 标注文件, data_path: 媒体目录或 ""}
  ├─ CAMBRIAN_737K_PACK = {...}   # packed 数据集也是同样的两键结构
  ├─ MP_DOC / CLEVR_MC / VIDEOCHATGPT = {...}
  └─ data_dict = { "cambrian_737k": CAMBRIAN_737K, ... }   # 代号 → 配置 的总表
```

分工的判断口诀：

| 情况 | data_path 该填什么 |
| --- | --- |
| 标注里是相对路径（如 `demo/images/10095.png`） | 相对路径的基准目录（如 `/xxx/qwen-vl-finetune`） |
| 标注里是绝对路径或 `file://` 路径 | 留空 `""` |

注意一个细节：`data_path` 为空时，相对路径会以**运行训练时的工作目录**为基准解析（后文 4.3 会看到 `Path("")` 的行为），所以最稳妥的做法是要么给足 `data_path`，要么标注里写绝对路径。

### 4.2 data_list 解析与 %X 采样率语法

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`data_list` 是注册表的查询函数：输入一组「可能带 `%X` 后缀」的数据集名字，输出一组**可直接使用的配置字典**，每个字典额外多一个 `sampling_rate` 键（浮点数 0~1）。它做三件事：

1. 用正则从名字末尾剥出 `%X`，换算成 `X / 100`；
2. 去掉后缀得到纯代号，去 `data_dict` 查表；
3. 查到的配置**浅拷贝**一份，挂上 `sampling_rate` 后收集返回；查不到就抛 `ValueError: do not find ...`。

采样发生在**解析之后、训练之前**的加载阶段（见 4.3），`data_list` 本身不读任何文件。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
输入: ["my_dataset%50", "clevr_mc"]
  对每个名字 name:
    rate = parse_sampling_rate(name)        # 正则 r"%(\d+)$" 命中末尾 %50 → 0.5；未命中 → 1.0
    name  = 去掉末尾 %50                     # "my_dataset"
    config = data_dict[name].copy()          # 浅拷贝，不污染注册表
    config["sampling_rate"] = rate
输出: [ {annotation_path, data_path, sampling_rate: 0.5},
       {annotation_path, data_path, sampling_rate: 1.0} ]
```

采到的样本条数公式（在 4.3 的加载阶段计算）：

\[ n_{sampled} = \operatorname{int}\left( N \times rate \right) \]

注意 `int()` 是**向下取整**：3 条样本 × 50% = 1.5 → 取 1 条。

必须掌握的四个边界情况：

| 写法 | 解析结果 | 后果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `my_dataset%50` | rate=0.5 | 正常用一半 |
| `my_dataset%150` | rate=1.5 | 解析不报错；加载时 `random.sample(annotations, k>N)` 抛 `ValueError` |
| `my_dataset%0` | rate=0.0 | 该数据集贡献 0 条样本（`random.sample(..., 0)` 返回空列表） |
| `my_dataset%50v2` | 正则要求 `%数字` 在**末尾**，不命中 | 整串 `my_dataset%50v2` 当作代号查表 → `do not find` |

另有一个易踩的坑：`dataset_use` 用逗号分隔多个名字时**不要加空格**。`"a,b"` 没问题，`"a, b"` 会把 `" b"`（带前导空格）当代号去查表而失败。此外 `random.sample` 没有固定随机种子，**同一命令两次运行抽到的子集不同**，做对比实验时需自行在训练脚本里 `random.seed(...)`（待本地验证：`train_qwen.py` 未额外设种子，跨 run 不可复现）。

### 4.3 LazySupervisedDataset 加载：从 dataset_use 到 list_data_dict

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`LazySupervisedDataset` 是训练时真正的数据集类（继承 `torch.utils.data.Dataset`）。它的 `__init__` 完成「从字符串到样本清单」的全部工作：

- 把 `data_args.dataset_use` 按逗号拆开，交给 4.2 的 `data_list` 得到配置列表；
- 逐个配置读标注文件（JSONL 逐行、JSON 整体）；
- 对 `sampling_rate < 1.0` 的数据集执行 `random.sample` 随机抽取；
- 给**每条标注**注入 `data_path` 键（后面 `_build_messages` 用它解析相对媒体路径）；
- 把所有数据集的标注按注册顺序**顺序拼接**成 `self.list_data_dict`。

「Lazy」体现在：到此为止**不做任何分词与图片读取**，只持有轻量的标注字典列表；`__len__` 就是 `len(list_data_dict)`，真正的张量化发生在训练循环按索引调用 `__getitem__` 时（u5-l3 精读）。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
__init__(processor, data_args)
  ├─ dataset_use.split(",")            # "a%50,b" → ["a%50", "b"]
  ├─ data_list(名字列表)               # 查表 + 解析采样率（4.2）
  ├─ for data in 配置列表:
  │    ├─ 后缀 == "jsonl" ? read_jsonl : json.load      # 按扩展名二分
  │    ├─ sampling_rate < 1.0 ?
  │    │     random.sample(annotations, int(N × rate))  # 在这里才真正采样
  │    └─ for ann in annotations:
  │         ann["data_path"] = data["data_path"]         # 逐条注入基准路径
  │         （ann 是 list 时对每个子项注入 → packed 样本，见 4.4）
  │    list_data_dict += annotations                     # 顺序拼接
  ├─ 打印 "Total training samples: N"
  ├─ update_processor_pixels(...)       # 把像素预算参数写进 processor（u5-l3 展开）
  └─ data_packing ? item_fn=_get_packed_item : item_fn=_get_item   # 决定取样本方式
```

`data_path` 注入是被下一讲反复引用的关键一步：标注文件里的相对路径之所以能被解析，就是因为加载时每条样本都随身携带了基准目录。`_build_messages` 中用 `Path(source.get("data_path", ""))` 取出它、再与相对路径拼接（参见 [qwen-vl-finetune/qwenvl/data/data_processor.py:L140-L156](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/qwen-vl-finetune/qwenvl/data/data_processor.py#L140-L156) 中的 `_make_abs_paths` 调用）。`data_path` 为空时 `Path("")` 退化为相对当前工作目录解析——这就是 4.1 说「留空需谨慎」的原因。

### 4.4 多数据集混合、packed 嵌套注入与长度属性

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

真实 SFT 往往混合多个数据集。本框架的混合规则非常朴素：

- **顺序拼接**：按 `dataset_use` 里代号的书写顺序，逐个数据集把标注 `+=` 到总列表。谁写在前面，谁的样本就排在列表前部。
- **逐数据集采样**：`%X` 只作用于它修饰的那一个代号，互不影响。
- **packed 样本兼容**：若某个数据集的标注是「桶的列表、桶内又是样本的列表」（u4-l2 讲过的两层结构），加载循环会把 `data_path` 注入到**每个内层子样本**上，保证后续逐样本处理时基准路径不丢失。

另外，`__init__` 会依据 `data_args.data_packing` 决定取样本的函数 `item_fn`：开 packing 时用 `_get_packed_item`（整桶取出），否则用 `_get_item`（单样本取出）。这与 u4-l4 的 `pack_data.py` 产出物配套。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
dataset_use = "a%50,b_pack"
list_data_dict = [a 的 5 条] + [b_pack 的若干「桶」(每桶是 list)]
                        ↑ 顶层元素类型不统一？没关系：
                          data_packing=True 时 _get_packed_item 把「桶」整体取出再逐样本处理
                          data_packing=False 时 _get_item 期望顶层元素是普通样本 dict
```

3. **需要观察的现象**：列表前部是来自 `my_dataset` 的普通样本 dict，随后出现来自 `my_dataset_pack` 的「桶」（list），桶内**每个**子样本都带上了相同的 `data_path`。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
